newsitem.title: LUXEMBOURG: Court says member states must accept EU rules on new cars.
newsitem.headline: Court says member states must accept EU rules on new cars.

text.p: The European Court of Justice said on Thursday Sweden cannot require cars, legally certified under Community rules, to pass Swedish exhaust emission standards before granting national registration.

An agent for Audi and Volkswagen challenged the Stockholm County Administrative Board when it refused to register a new Audi A4, even though the car was properly certified under a Community-type approval system.

The intent of the Swedish law is to provide new car buyers with protection against manufacturer liability, according to the judgment. The court noted that the information required for Swedish certification complies broadly with the information required under Community rules.
The court said that except where a car is a serious risk to road safety, member states cannot refuse to register new cars covered by a valid Community type-approval certificate.
Reference by the Lansratten i Stockholms lan (Sweden) for a preliminary ruling brought by

on the interpretation of Council directive 70/156/EEC on the approximation of the laws of the member states relating to the type-approval of motor vehicles and their trailers and article 30 and 36 of the EC treaty

Council directive 70/156/EEC on the approximation of the laws of the member states relating to the type-approval of motor vehicles and their trailers, as amended, must be interpreted as precluding national legislation under which motor vehicles covered by a valid Community type-approval certificate cannot be registered unless a national certificate is produced attesting to their conformity with national requirements concerning exhaust emissions.
